title: JuliusBrussee/caveman: shorter agent talk, same code, author's own numbers
friendlyTitle: A tool that makes a coding agent talk less
summary: Caveman is an open skill and proxy that tells a coding agent to say less and read less, while leaving the code unchanged. The repository now also promotes Caveman Code, a desktop app the author says runs on subscriptions and keys you already have. On the author's November runs, one test cut input tokens by 33.2 percent across 54 Claude Code sessions, with the answers still marked correct. GitHub Trending listed it with 227 stars today.
friendlySummary: Caveman is an open skill and a middle layer that tells a coding agent to use fewer words and read less extra text. The code itself is meant to stay the same. The author now also offers a desktop app, and says one of their own tests cut input text by about a third. It gained 227 stars on GitHub today.
whyItMatters: Add the skill or proxy when a coding agent is spending the bill on chatter and bulky tool output. Treat the savings percentages as the project's own measurements, not an independent audit. The part to check is the claim that code stays exact while the surrounding language gets shorter.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Use it when a coding agent is wasting money on long chatter and huge tool replies. The savings numbers are the author's own tests, not an outside check. Look closely at whether the code really stays unchanged while the talk around it gets shorter.
